{"decision":"RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-09-26, dev_reflow2 hub session, "as a distant idea":

"use the jira API to automatically build jira tasks for decisions in the graph that need to be made, gaps that need to be settled, requirements that are unsatisfied, etc. basically, the agent automatically builds jira tasks for based on the graph. In the image (from flo2.io), the open items would become jira tasks."

The image was flo2.io's account page for the backyard greenhouse design: requirements marked PROPOSED (backup heater for winter, greenhouse frame material, fish tank held between 20 and 24 °C, grow beds drain fully within ten minutes of pump shutdown, gutters feed rain barrel, run two weeks unattended, backup air pump on a separate circuit, low-water float switch cuts the pump), one DEFERRED, one DROPPED; components PLANNED (300-gallon fish tank, sump pump, UV clarifier); a constraint.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS TO FEED IT: the design already computes exactly this worklist. loop_status lists what the loop is owed; open_questions, detect_gaps and gap_to_prompt rank the gaps and phrase each as a question; proposed Decisions and proposed Requirements are queryable; a Decision assigned to a person carries an approver edge (req:an-assigned-open-decision-is-reported). What is missing is only the push into a tracker, and keeping the two in step.

═══ OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN ═══
(a) NO CODE: A SKILL, AND ATLASSIAN'S OWN MCP SERVER. The agent already has reflow2's worklist; with a Jira connector beside it, a served skill ("turn the open items into Jira tasks") tells it what to create and how to keep it idempotent. CHEAPEST. Needs only the skill and a stable key per item.
(b) ONE-WAY PUSH WITH A MAPPING: each task carries its design node's id (a label or issue property such as reflow2:req:backup-heater); re-running updates rather than duplicates, and when the item settles in the design its task is moved to Done. SMALL on top of (a).
(c) TWO-WAY: Jira changes flow back. See pushback: a closed ticket cannot settle a design decision.
(d) HOSTED IN flo2: flo2 holds each design's Jira connection (Atlassian OAuth, per design) and syncs on every change, with no agent in the loop. LARGEST: a stored third-party credential, a background job, per-design opt-in.
(e) A NEUTRAL WORKLIST EXPORT in reflow2 (one call returning "what needs a person", grouped and ranked), with small adapters for Jira, GitHub Issues or Linear outside reflow2. Keeps reflow2 free of any network I/O, and serves every tracker, not just Jira.

═══ PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT ═══
· 🛑 THE DESIGN STAYS THE TRUTH; JIRA IS A VIEW. A Decision is settled and a Requirement accepted only on the owner's word (rule:design-intent-moves-only-on-the-owners-word). So closing a Jira task must never settle anything in the design; at most it asks the owner. Status flows design → Jira, not back. This is why (c) is recorded but risky.
· VOLUME. reflow2's own design has 117 open gaps today, flo2's 96. One task per gap would bury a board. The push should take only what needs a PERSON: open decisions (especially assigned ones), requirements awaiting confirmation, accepted requirements nothing satisfies, and gaps above a severity line, grouped, not one per finding.
· DESIGN QUESTIONS AND BUILD WORK ARE DIFFERENT TASKS. In the image, "PROPOSED" requirements are "confirm this wording" tasks for the owner, while "PLANNED" components (the sump pump, the UV clarifier) are "buy or build this" work. Both could go to Jira, but as different issue types, and the second is delivery tracking, which the design only records.
· STABLE KEYS. Gap ids are derived from their content and can change as wording changes, which would duplicate tasks. The key should be the node id plus the kind of item.
· WHO. A Jira assignee has to come from somewhere: the approver on an assigned Decision, mapped Contributor → Jira account. That map does not exist.
· PRIVACY IS PER DESIGN. Pushing a design's open items to a third-party tracker publishes its content there. cure, a personal medical design, must never be synced; it has to be an opt-in per design, never a default.
· reflow2 DOES NO NETWORK I/O, by principle. The Jira call belongs to the agent, a script or flo2, never inside reflow2 itself.

A FINDING, NOT A DECISION: (a) plus (b) is a skill and a naming convention, and would show within a week whether a board of design questions actually helps.
